freshness_note: Every citation on a mover, volume outlier, or recommendation card carries the actual publish date of its source, separate from this page's pull date above. Price/volume/index data always refreshes live on pull; narrative research is only rewritten when genuinely newer reporting was found for that name - otherwise the existing writeup stands rather than being re-presented under a fresher-looking timestamp. The 11/18/26 pull reflects the Wed Nov 18 session - equity data is current through that close, with no data lag (market-cap filter cache refreshed 11/18/26). It is the first pull since 11/02/26, so the market backdrop includes the Nov 5 post-midterm AI crash, Jensen Huang's Nov 12 resignation as Nvidia CEO and a five-day S&P 500 losing streak. Four themes drive the Nov 18 movers: (1) a cybersecurity rally (PANW, QLYS, OKTA, CRWD, ATEN) after a Nov 17 CISA alert on an AI-discovered Java flaw and DHS testimony on AI-powered attacks; (2) managed care fell (UNH -10%, ELV, HUM, MOH) after CMS proposed a Medicare Advantage/Medicaid anti-fraud audit rule on Nov 18; (3) gold, silver and copper miners (NEM, CDE, HL, FCX) fell as gold hit a 14-month low on Fed-hike bets and a strong dollar, and refiners (CVI, DINO, PARR, PBF) fell as oil dropped more than 4%; (4) retail earnings beats lifted TJX and Target. Nvidia fell 2.9% despite beating on Nov 17. AES's volume spike is merger arbitrage on its $15 take-private, not a trading signal, and its speculative card is marked a false positive. Corteva's recommendation card is rewritten: its drop is a real Nov 11 guidance cut, not the spin-off artifact described earlier. Names marked "no clean catalyst" (WRBY, PRGO, SGI, CAKE, RGEN, DVA, MGEE) had no dated reporting explaining the move. value.name: Insulet Corporation
value.thesis: UPDATE (11/18/26): Insulet's Nov 4 Q3 report beat: revenue was $842M (+19.2%), adjusted EPS $1.99 (+59.9%, about 25% above consensus), and 2026 guidance was raised to 21-22% constant-currency growth. But the preliminary 2027 outlook calls for growth modestly below its mid-teens framework, with U.S. growth toward the low end of 9-14%. Management said type-2 retention improved only modestly despite its action plan, while Omnipod Discover passed 35,000 users. The shares have since slid to about $140 from roughly $157 before the report. The value case is intact on margins and buybacks (about $400M planned in Q4), but the retention fix that the case depends on is not yet showing up. Prior framing: Two dated items since Oct 1. (1) Oct 12: Jefferies kept Buy but cut its target to $190 from $275, reportedly on competition concerns (Quiver Quant, AI-generated summary citing Investing.com) - consistent with the 2027 tubeless-AID competition risk below; the stock still rose ~3.3% that day. (2) Oct 17: Simply Wall St reports Omnipod Discover is now in full U.S. market release after a pre-launch with 15,000+ Omnipod 5 users and 1,800+ HCPs - the retention tool this value case depends on is live, though it calls the rollout incremental and says the real test is type-2 utilization stabilizing. Next print expected early November. Insulet is down over 60% from its 52-week high after an August 2026 guidance cut, but management's own explanation points to a fixable operational issue rather than collapsing core demand: about two-thirds of the cut traced to weaker type-2 diabetes customer retention and utilization in the first 90 days of therapy, with the remainder from slower new-customer starts and pricing mix - not competitive share loss. The real risk ahead is that tubeless automated-insulin-delivery competitors are expected to enter the market in 2027, which could pressure both share and pricing. Value case depends on retention tools (Omnipod Discover) fixing the 90-day drop-off before competition arrives.
